title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
abstract: arXiv:2610.32969v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. translated_title: DexPort：一种用于灵巧手数据采集的手持式技能接口
translated_abstract: 收集高质量的演示数据仍然是学习灵巧操作的核心瓶颈。遥操作能够记录可执行的机器人动作，但它需要完整的机器人设备，并把协调众多手指关节的负担压在操作者身上。人类演示更容易收集，但其动作必须经过估计并重定向到机器人，而且不能直接提供机器人动作。在本文中，我们提出了DexPort，一个面向高自由度机器人手的便携式数据采集接口。它在数据采集与部署时使用相同的手部硬件，从而避免了手部实体差异（embodiment gap），并同时记录指令关节目标和测量关节状态。我们的关键观察是：一小组技能就可以支持广泛的灵巧任务。在采集过程中，操作者移动手持接口来指定机器人手腕运动，并选择或调整协调手指运动的技能。（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: DexPort提出了一种面向高自由度灵巧手的便携式手持数据采集接口，通过采集与部署共用相同手部硬件来避免实体差异，并借助一小组可选择的技能来协调手指运动，从而大幅降低高质量灵巧操作演示数据的采集成本。
en_tdlr: DexPort is a portable hand-held data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands that uses the same hand hardware for both collection and deployment to avoid the embodiment gap, and relies on a small set of selectable skills to coordinate finger motions, greatly reducing the cost of collecting high-quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.
